Unfortunately, this place felt more like a trap than a good dining experience.

We visited as a family, two adults and two young children (3.5 years and 7 months old), and spent $150+ on two curries, two naans, a beer and a cocktail, and maybe one more finger food The prices felt seriously inflated for the quality of food. We came here after the previous restaurant we were looking for had a notice on its door directing customers here. When we asked, we were told this was the same business under a different name. Whether that was actually the case, I don't know, but it definitely influenced our decision to dine here. To add to the disappointment, our seven-month-old accidentally dropped a small plate and I was charged $20. I understand accidents happen and that restaurants may charge for breakages, but $20 felt excessive. I had to ask what that additional unexplained cost was. The duty manager explained that he was too generous not to charge us actual $30.

The atmosphere is nice, but for the food and prices, I wouldn't return. If you're after ambience, perhaps give it a try. If you're after good food and value, I'd look elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very poor vehicle quality control and disappointing after-sales service from David Wang.

We’ve had to take the car back to the dealership three times for the same issue, which has been extremely frustrating.

On the day we picked up the car, it rained and we noticed straight away that the windscreen became blurry when the wipers were used. We brought the car back to the dealership to have the windscreen treated. After that, a new problem appeared — the wiper judders and skips when it reaches the upper-right corner of the windscreen, especially when the glass is not very wet (you can hear it if you turn the sound on).

We contacted David Wang about the issue, but were told that most of their cars have the same problem and that it’s normal. To be honest, this was very disappointing. If this is a common issue with their vehicles, we believe customers should be told about it before making a purchase.

After going back and forth, David agreed to have us bring the car back again. He also agreed to our request to speak with the manager. However, when we turned up at the dealership, neither David nor the manager was there. We were left dealing with another salesperson.

We bought the car expecting a reasonable level of quality and after-sales support. Instead, we’ve had to make three trips back to the dealership just to deal with one issue, and we still don’t feel that it has been properly resolved.

Based on our experience, we would not recommend this brand or this dealership. The vehicle quality control has been disappointing, and the after-sales service has been even more frustrating.

We will also consider taking this matter further and raising our concerns with the relevant authorities.

I’m writing this on behalf of my two sisters, who recently visited Bargain Chemist at WestCity. They told me that one staff member approached them and asked whether they needed help. Even after they politely said they were fine, the staff member continued following them through the store, repeatedly pretending to tidy products near wherever they were standing. Another employee also appeared to watch their every move.

What made the experience especially upsetting was that other customers were warmly greeted when they entered, while my sisters felt they were being watched and treated with suspicion. As two young brown women, they were left wondering whether they were being singled out because of their appearance. They became so uncomfortable that they left without buying anything.

No customer should be made to feel unwelcome or treated like a potential thief simply for browsing. I hope management takes this seriously, speaks with the staff involved, and ensures every customer is treated with the same warmth, dignity, and respect.

Went there with my sister and one of the workers, approached us asking if we needed help and after we said we were okay she continues to follow us and pretending to be busy sorting things out that were already in perfect order, the longer we stayed the more workers seemed to join in on keeping an eye on us. More customers came in and they greeted them nicely. The racial profiling has to stop because we just wanted to get things we needed but we ended up leaving because of how uncomfortable we felt.
